contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Guard selected wave-step starts and refresh progress/statistics within a local transaction.
inputs_defaults: waveNum numeric(9), processStamp nvarchar(100), userStamp nvarchar(30), nextStep nvarchar(25); required, no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Missing/NULL wave can leave warehouse NULL and bypass equality conflicts, then update no target. Unknown/NULL nextStep bypasses the coded guarded branches; it is still assigned if target constraints permit. NULL previous current step is normalized by the coded last-step expression.
output_shape: Explicit integer returns are zero on gate rejection and on the ordinary post-COMMIT @@ROWCOUNT path; they do not distinguish a successful update count. No intentional result set.

ordered_branches.explanation: BEGIN TRANSACTION. Read warehouse for this wave using NOLOCK.

For either of two coded next-step tokens, acquire TABLOCKX via existence check for another wave in the same warehouse running either guarded token. For a third token, check its corresponding conflicting token. Conflict rolls back and returns zero.

Test the latest @@ERROR; on nonzero roll back and return zero. Update statistics totals, START_DATE_TIME only when previously NULL, END_DATE_TIME to UTC now, LAST_LAUNCH_STEP from prior current-step mapping, CURRENT_LAUNCH_STEP to nextStep, and stamps.
COMMIT TRANSACTION, then RETURN @@ROWCOUNT. COMMIT resets this value to zero under documented SQL Server behavior.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Writes progress timestamps and summary totals; END_DATE_TIME here is refreshed on each call, not proof of completed warehouse execution.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: Guards are hard-coded step-token comparisons, not a complete wave-master step engine. Exact token meanings remain unpublished and are not inferred from the method name. Existing unit labels are preserved; missing ones use MAX source label.
error_and_return_handling: No TRY/CATCH, XACT_ABORT declaration, rowcount-before-COMMIT capture or comprehensive post-UPDATE error check. Return zero alone cannot prove success; statement errors can propagate.
contract.transaction_ownership: Explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION, COMMIT and unqualified ROLLBACK in gate/error branches. No @@TRANCOUNT ownership test or savepoint; a rollback can unwind a caller transaction. Nested commit does not independently commit an outer transaction.
concurrency: TABLOCKX is a table-level exclusive lock, broader than one wave/warehouse. It is used only in guarded branches. The earlier warehouse read and NOLOCK shipment aggregates are not a complete snapshot.
contract.trigger_behavior: No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger on these target tables is present in the captured six-trigger inventory, except SHIPPING_CONTAINER has an INSERT-only trigger and WORK_INSTRUCTION has an INSERT-only trigger; updates/deletes here do not directly activate those INSERT events. Constraints and caller actions still apply.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application interpretation of zero, caller transaction nesting, step-token semantics and restart rules remain external. Static return analysis is not an executed defect reproduction.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
Owner backup/leftover and item-master-failure suggestions are hypotheses. Name patterns and missing references do not validate them. No deletion recommendation is made.
Current replica status is owner-attested. This task documents the captured source as-is and requires no application version/build or extension development.
